Port Vila City Council runs the cemetery and plot reservations; old cemetery full, new Eratap cemetery opened. Funeral trade is one or two firms (Vanuatu Funerals Ltd took over Defloor, https://vbr.vu/news/vanuatu-funerals-takes-over-defloor-expands-embalming-and-repatriation-services/). Building Act 2013 (No. 36) needs a building permit from an Approval Authority with a certificate from an approved building certifier; the Director General of Internal Affairs keeps the certifier register; Vanuatu National Building Code 2025 edition and Building Regulations 2025 mentioned, in-force status unverified (https://duap.gov.vu/images/docs/VNBC%202025%20Edition.pdf). Quarry Act 2013 (No. 9) sets prospecting, quarry and occasional permits issued by the Commissioner of Mines, with environment and rehabilitation plans (https://pacliirms.paclii.org/vu/legis/num_act/qa2013115). All buyer groups are very small.

result.competitor: No dedicated software, app or done-for-you service found for kava facility QM records or export documents in Vanuatu or Fiji. Existing resources: the PHAMA Plus Kava Quality Manual (paper guidance), the KavaLytics testing device/service (quality testing, not records), and the Vanuatu trade portal (lists steps only). Bislama/French-language search not run.
result.duty: Kava Act No.7 of 2002 as amended by Kava (Amendment) Act No.6 of 2015 (export licence under Part 3A, renewal by application to the Director, in force 24 Jan 2017; penalty clause not reached). Biosecurity OPS-014 Kava Quality Management Procedures (Export): facility certification after inspection, then VCMB licence, annual facility audit; peeling, ~5% moisture, kavalactone/flavokavin testing with high-flavokavin lots rejected. Industry reminder issued 3 Aug 2026. Record-keeping requirements in OPS-014 not verified (the public page doesn't mention them).
result.market: Very small. A Daily Post article says Santo kava exporters fell from 14 to 12 (undated in results; the page returned 429). Australian Commercial Kava Pilot data, as reported in search results, lists 45 Vanuatu exporters (Oct 2022), and a Daily Post article says 48. Eight exporters ship to New Caledonia. No current national register count was found. A likely total of roughly 30–60 certified exporters is my estimate, not a sourced figure.
result.reason: I confirmed the duty, but the market is very small. Biosecurity Vanuatu requires each facility to be certified under OPS-014, then licensed by VCMB, then audited every year. Kava must be peeled, hold about 5% moisture and pass kavalactone/flavokavin tests. Biosecurity repeated this in a reminder on 3 Aug 2026. Under the Kava (Amendment) Act 2015, in force since Jan 2017, exporting needs a licence and the licence must be renewed. I could not see the penalty clause. No public source I found says OPS-014 requires batch records. I found no kava batch-record or export-document software, only PHAMA's paper Kava Quality Manual and KavaLytics testing. Exporters number only dozens (12 in Santo; 45–48 Vanuatu exporters in Australia's pilot in 2022), so few buyers and weak willingness to pay. A traceability premium (KavaLytics says about 20%) is the possible upside.

Duty is real: DCIR guidance says licences renew each calendar year by 31 January, fees are based on prior-year gross turnover, and late payment carries a 10% monthly penalty. I did not read the Act text for the penalty. I found no Vanuatu compliance calendar or reminder app, and no online renewal portal. The new eBusiness Link covers registration only. Weak points: I found no business count (no licence totals from DCIR or the national statistics office), payment is in person at DCIR, buyers are very small and offline, and willingness to pay is low. The duty is annual, so a reminder tool has little recurring value. A calendar or reminder tool is thin and hard to charge for.

Duty is real: Co-operative Societies Act Cap 152 Part 6 has annual returns (s35), audit (s36) and Registrar inspection/inquiry (ss37-38), plus the 1987 Rules on accounts and audit. I could not read the section text, so deadlines and penalties are not verified. Market is 460 co-ops with 17,428 members (ICAP 2025 snapshot), with tiny revenue (about $8.6M across 113 reporting co-ops) and an unknown number of active ones. No local software or state portal found, but only 3 searches were run and none were Vanuatu-specific. Willingness to pay is very low, buyers are scattered across islands, and the Registrar's office is likely the only payer, which makes this a state or donor build and out of scope. Score is low.

The duty is real. The AML/CTF Act 13 of 2014, consolidated through 2024 amendments, requires covered entities to register with the FIU before trading (s9). They must also appoint a compliance officer, do customer due diligence, and file STR/CTR/IFTR reports. Covered sectors per FIU press releases (2016, 2021): money exchange and remittance, real estate, high-value dealers over VT1m, and lawyers/accountants managing client property. No competing local product turned up, and the FIU registration looks paper-form based. But the market is tiny, probably a few hundred entities, with no count found. Willingness to pay is low and the FIU's own guidance is free. Reports are low volume, and the filing channel is unknown. Penalty amounts (VT25m claimed) were not verified. Score stays at 3.

AML reporting duty on small law, real estate and money-changer offices; in scope as small professional offices.

Employment Act annual return and work permits; K03 is the VNPF schedule, a different duty (related K03).

Fisheries licences and export permits for small processors are a new duty; unverified.
